# Sibling-holds e2e finds no Audit header when its sampler starts

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabDragSiblingHoldsNL.spec.mjs` (#20074, for #20072) has failed twice with the same symptom:
- **2026-10-23:** Ada, while qualifying #20083, ran the grid and workstation NL tier: "a sampler race in WorkstationTabDragSiblingHoldsNL, 3/3 head + 3/3 base in isolation".
- **2026-10-26:** on the contributor PR #20119, Brain E2E shard 2/10 (run 40277307605, job 121458090653) failed at `:59` with `page.evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')`. The identical spec blob `affff65e` passed on `dev` `056f5493` with the same Brain pin, so #20119's diff is not implicated.

## The Problem

Before the drag, the spec resolves the sibling's header id through `getTabChromeIdentity('right-top-tabs')` and the element is found (`page.locator('#' + chrome.buttons.audit).boundingBox()` succeeds). It then sets a 4× CPU throttle, starts dragging Metrics, waits for `.neo-tab-header-toolbar.neo-is-dragging`, moves 300 px below the strip, and only then looks the sibling up again inside `page.evaluate` (`document.getElementById(id)`). On a failing run that lookup returns `null`, so the pre-drag id has no element in the DOM at that moment.

Two readings remain, and they lead to different fixes:
- **(a) A product defect.** Under load, the Audit header leaves the DOM or is re-rendered at drag start, so a user would see the sibling tab blink. This is the kind of sibling disruption the spec exists to forbid.
- **(b) A test artifact.** The sibling persists, but its element identity changes between the pre-drag resolution and the sampler.

## The Architectural Reality

- The spec reads the chrome identity through the Neural Link (`app.callMethod(workspaceId, 'getTabChromeIdentity', [NODE])`) and the DOM through `page.evaluate`. The sampler captures `header` once and samples `getBoundingClientRect().x` every animation frame.
- The disappearance happens inside the dock's tab-drag start path under throttle. Which component re-renders the strip there is not established yet; that is the first deliverable below.

## The Fix

1. Discriminate first. Instrument the sampler to re-resolve the sibling every frame and, on a frame where the id is absent, record the strip's header-button ids and classes. Reproduce under the spec's 4× throttle (`--repeat-each`) on `dev`.
2. **For (a):** fix the drag-start path so the sibling header keeps its element, and make the spec fail on any frame where the sibling is absent.
3. **For (b):** the spec resolves the sibling by its stable identity on every frame; no product change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a reproduction receipt names which case occurs: run count, null-frame count, and what the strip held on a null frame.
- [ ] AC-2: the fix for that case lands; for (a), a red-first spec arm shows the absent sibling on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3: the spec treats an absent sibling as a failure rather than a `TypeError`, and passes 20/20 under the 4× throttle at the fix head.

**AC-1 reproduction (2026-10-26, `dev` `4eb27683fb`, Brain `origin/dev` `16cfb23b`, own Bridge on a free port): case (a), a product defect.**

I instrumented the sampler locally to re-resolve the sibling every frame and to snapshot the strip on any frame where it is missing, then ran it `--repeat-each=10` under the spec's 4× throttle. Result: **9 passed, 1 failed**.

- In the 9 passes, `neo-tab-header-button-17` (Audit) is present on all 84–85 sampled frames.
- In the failing run it is absent on **all 89 frames**, from the first sample through the whole sweep, about 1.5 s. On those frames the DOM holds the original Metrics button (`neo-tab-header-button-16` in `neo-tab-header-toolbar-5`, which carries `neo-is-dragging`) and its proxy clone (`neo-vnode-627` in `neo-dragproxy-1`). **No element anywhere carries the "Evidence Audit" text**, so this is not an identity change: the sibling tab is out of the DOM while Metrics is dragged.

Lead, not yet confirmed: `TabSortZone#expandOwnerOnDrag` documents that the toolbar's Overflow plugin can misclassify a tab as space-hidden when the owner's width changes during the gesture. A throttled frame that measures the strip mid-drag-start could hide Audit the same way. Next: read `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` against the drag-start path, add the Audit button's `hidden`/`removeDom` state and the Overflow verdict to the failing-frame snapshot, then write the red arm.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-26T17:06:37Z

**AC-1, the mechanism (2026-10-26, `dev` 40738ff6b1).** Case (a) has one cause, and it starts at the press, not at the drag.

1. The press focuses the pane, and its five focus-gated actions reveal: first at 0 px, then rendered at 24 px each. In this 220 px strip that leaves 76 px for Metrics (55 px, active and focused) and Audit (48 px), so the next Overflow pass withholds Audit.
2. If the drag's snapshot comes first, that pass is deferred and Audit stays. That is the spec's usual case, because its press lasts about 10 ms: in 40 instrumented runs (a trace of every Overflow pass, read back through the Neural Link), the drag won every time.
3. A press that rests 400 ms before the drag, as a person's does, loses that race 5 of 5 times. Audit is withheld about 230 ms after the press. The drag then drops focus to the body and the actions withdraw, but the frozen partition keeps Audit out for the whole sweep.

**The fix (`grace/20128-sibling-stays-at-drag-start`, PR linked below):** `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` holds the owner's focus-gated reveal for a primary tab press, the shape #20052 gave the press on its control. The click, a leave before the press drags, or the release of the drag it became applies the owed reveal. The spec gains the resting press as a second arm (red on `dev` 3/3) and resolves the header on every frame, so a missing one fails as such (AC-3: 40/40 at the head).

**Correction to my handover above:** port 18091 was not free. Another seat's Neural Link Bridge has listened there since 10-24, so those runs were not on their own Bridge. Today's receipts ran on 18191.

revealed actions, the Overflow pass then withheld the unprotected sibling,
and a drag starting from the press froze it out of the strip for the whole
gesture, although the drag drops focus and withdraws those actions.

as it already does for a press on its control. The click, a leave before
the press drags, or the release of the drag it became ends the hold. The
owner DOM listeners come from one list that registration and release share.

that rests 400 ms before the drag: red on dev 3/3."
